Done. The plan at `out/T1/plan.yaml` ran with exit code 0 and wrote `out/T1/model.safetensors`.

What the plan does:
- Asserts the input has 244 tensors, then deletes every tensor of blocks 2, 6, 10 and 14 with one regex `delete`.
- Renumbers the ten shifted blocks with regex `move` transforms in ascending old-index order, so each destination is always free before it is written.
- Ends with an `all` assertion covering the required checks: no tensor of blocks 12 to 15 exists, exactly 12 `query_key_value.weight` tensors, exactly 180 block tensors in indices 0 to 11, and 184 tensors total.

Executions: 2, both successful. The second was an identical re-run only to capture the exit code, because I had truncated the first run's log. The self-report is in `out/T1/REPORT.md`, and it notes the one documentation gap I hit: the `move` help does not show a capture-group example, so regex rewrite support is inferred from the `assert: equal` section of the README.
